pr_title: Fix multiple attributes usage in conjunction with OpenRegion. Fixes #16570
pr_body:
Each of the scope-opening methods (`OpenElement`, `OpenComponent`, `OpenRegion`) is meant to do a bit of housekeeping related to `AddMultipleAttributes`.

However it seems that `OpenRegion` had been missed out, and the necessary logic had only been applied to `OpenElement` and `OpenComponent`. This resulted in duplicated attributes that confused the diff and produced overall strangeness as seen in #16570.

issue_context.title: InputSelect loses class attribute when setting disabled equals true
issue_context.body:
### If you believe you have an issue that affects the security of the platform please do NOT create an issue and instead email your issue details to secure@microsoft.com. Your report may be eligible for our [bug bounty](https://technet.microsoft.com/en-us/mt764065.aspx) but ONLY if it is reported through email.

### Describe the bug
InputSelect component loses it's class attribute when setting disabled attribute to true, e.g.

`<InputSelect disabled="@(isRemoved)">...</InputSelect>`

### To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Using this version of ASP.NET Core 3.1 preview and Visual Studio preview

### Expected behavior
The component should not drop class attribute for the select control. I've not seen other input components having the same behavior.

### Additional context
Add any other context about the problem here.
Include the output of `dotnet --info`

  Microsoft.NETCore.App 3.1.0-preview1.19506.1 [C:\Program Files\dotnet\shared\Microsoft.NETCore.App]

comments:
@jan-johansson-mr thanks for contacting us.

@SteveSandersonMS Do you know why this can be?
No, I don't know. It would be great to have a complete repro. The code posted above doesn't have any `class` attribute.

Hi,

I've just done an example, derived from the blazor server side template, that I've uploaded (solution with the source files), to show InputSelect dropping class when disabled.

Please have a look at the [example](https://github.com/jan-johansson-mr/BlazorExample).

Thanks

@jan-johansson-mr Thanks for the repro.

@SteveSandersonMS I did a quick check and unless I'm missing something I believe this is a bug. Do you want to take a look?

Well this is very surprising. We almost never get bugs in the actual rendering system, but this really is one. It requires a very particular combination of things to trigger it. Will be fixed in https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetCore/pull/16640
Thanks for a very quick resolution!!
